item.title: Democratic rep tells ABC, CBS to 'grow a spine' after Kimmel announces alternative Talarico interview
item.description: California Rep. Ted Lieu accused ABC and CBS of "bending the knee" after Jimmy Kimmel shifted his James Talarico interview off-air in a pair of deleted X posts.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Ted Lieu, D-Calif., attacked ABC, CBS and other networks in a pair of deleted X posts Thursday after hearing reports about Jimmy Kimmel's upcoming interview with Democratic Texas U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico.

The late-night host announced Wednesday night he would be interviewing Talarico. 

But, out of concern for the FCC under President Donald Trump, he added that he would be releasing the interview on YouTube instead of airing it on his show, "Jimmy Kimmel Live!"

Lieu accused ABC and other networks, like CBS, of "bending the knee" to authoritarians by refusing to air interviews of elected officials.

JIMMY KIMMEL RETURNS FROM LENGTHY HIATUS WITH DEFIANT MESSAGE TO FCC CHAIR BRENDAN CARR

"Dear @ABC, @CBS and other networks: Grow a f---ing spine. Air whatever interviews with elected officials you want. You will win in court. Bending the knee to an authoritarian Administration only makes things worse. I assume you will now never air an interview of Trump as well?" Lieu wrote.

"You know what else you can do @ABC and @CBS? Offer Ken Paxton the opportunity to come onto late night talk shows where the hosts can legitimately skewer Paxton by asking him about all his scandals. But instead you groveled and chose the path of self-censorship. Shameful."

Fox News Digital reached out to ABC, CBS and Lieu's office for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

Kimmel similarly accused the FCC of targeting his show and ABC based on "guest bookings it would seem they don’t like."

DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS

"Now that he’s president, his FCC has threatened me, threatened our show, threatened our network, ABC, our affiliates, our local stations, based on traditional simple editorial decisions, guest bookings it would seem they don’t like," Kimmel said.

"And, so, out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas who have to deal with this nonsense, my interview tomorrow with James Talarico will not air on television. It will be posted on YouTube instead. It will not be on TV."

The situation was reminiscent of former late-night host Stephen Colbert's interview with Talarico ahead of the Texas Senate primary, in which Talarico competed against Texas Rep. Jasmine Crockett.

Colbert's show, which has since been canceled, did not air the interview with Talarico and only posted it to the show's YouTube channel in February. Colbert announced at the time that CBS had stopped the show from airing the interview.

However, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr clarified to Fox News at the time that the interview would have potentially violated the equal-time rule, which requires broadcast stations to provide equal opportunities to opposing political candidates during an election season.

COLBERT LASHES OUT AT CBS, SAYS CANCELLATION ‘REINFORCED A NARRATIVE’ OF ‘KNEE BENDING’ TO TRUMP

In a comment to Fox News Digital, Curtis Houck, managing editor at NewsBusters, suggested Kimmel could land in "hot water" for his stunt to move around the equal-time rule and avoid speaking with Talarico's GOP opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

"Jimmy Kimmel thinks he's being cute or even brave by thumbing his nose at the FCC, but he's likely to end up in hot water for this. The equal time rules are what they are," Houck said.

"Kimmel and his clapping seals in the liberal, elitist media are telling on themselves when they try to explain away the record of Kimmel and his fellow network late-night hosts as virulent partisans with guest disparities that can only be rivaled by ABC's ‘The View.’" 

Fox News Digital also reached out to the FCC and Talarico and Paxton's respective campaigns for comment.

item.title: Spain basketball star Megan DiLeo weighs in on Caitlin Clark's World Cup bench role ahead of semifinal
item.description: Megan DiLeo helped recruit Caitlin Clark to Iowa, but now the Spain center aims to upset her former school's star in the FIBA World Cup semifinal.
item.content:encoded:
BERLIN — Megan DiLeo will be looking to lead Team Spain to an upset win over the U.S. in the FIBA Women's World Cup semifinal on Saturday. That means she will be taking on her old friend Caitlin Clark.

But DiLeo, Spain's star center and a 2025 WNBA champion with the Las Vegas Aces, may have to wait for Clark to come off the bench before seeing her on the hardwood. USA coach Kara Lawson has opted to start veteran Chelsea Gray over Clark at point guard for the U.S.'s first four games, despite Clark putting up superior numbers and playing more minutes.

But DiLeo doesn't believe that Clark not starting will make things any easier for Spain on Saturday.

TEAM USA COACH REVEALS IF CAITLIN CLARK WILL START IN THE WORLD CUP FINAL STAGE AFTER BENCH ROLE IN GROUP PLAY

When asked if Clark not starting on Saturday will put Team Spain at an advantage, DiLeo said, "No, I don't think so. She's just a great player, it doesn't really matter when she goes into a game, she's going to make an impact."

DiLeo added, "We just gotta be ready for her and for the rest of the roster. They're talented, they're deep. It kind of doesn't really matter who comes in."

Saturday will be a reunion for the two Iowa alumni, as DiLeo played for the Hawkeyes from 2015-19, before Clark showed up on campus one year later.

DiLeo said Friday that she helped recruit Clark to Iowa back then.

"I was actually part of the recruiting process that she was kind of going through, figuring out where she wanted to go, as far as that, and she chose Iowa," DiLeo said. "Whenever I go back to visit campus and stuff and she was still playing we would get to interact and stuff, we check in on eachother every once in a while now. Just super happy we get to represent Iowa."

DiLeo added that she hasn't spoken to Clark since they arrived in Germany for the World Cup due to scheduling constraints, but she's "excited" to see Clark on Saturday.

DiLeo won consensus National Player of the Year honors in 2019 and finished her college career with 2,804 points and a school-record 1,460 rebounds. Iowa later retired her No. 10.

Clark became a two-time consensus National Player of the Year and finished her career with 3,951 points, the most in NCAA Division I basketball history. She also led Iowa to consecutive national championship games before the school retired her No. 22.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Saturday will not be the first time they have faced each other internationally.

The U.S. defeated Spain 84-70 during the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico in March. DiLeo scored 15 points for Spain, while Clark finished with seven points and seven assists. Clark was later named the tournament’s most valuable player after leading the Americans to a 5-0 record.

DiLeo became a naturalized Spanish citizen in 2023 and made her debut for Spain at the 2024 Paris Olympics. She averaged 18 points and 9.3 rebounds during that tournament and has remained one of the country’s most important interior players.

She helped Spain reach Saturday’s semifinal with 16 points on 7-of-11 shooting during an 89-66 quarterfinal victory over Australia. Spain shot 50% from the field and made 13 3-pointers while eliminating the Opals.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Americans delivered an even more dominant quarterfinal performance. They defeated Hungary 108-56 while setting World Cup quarterfinal records for points and assists.

Clark scored 10 points and recorded a game-high nine assists in 20 minutes. She is now third among all players in assists per game at the tournament.

Her best performance came in the opening game against China, when she recorded 14 points and 11 assists without committing a turnover. She struggled during the Americans’ 55-52 escape against Italy but responded with nine points and seven assists against Czechia before nearly recording another double-double against Hungary.

Lawson has continued to use Clark with a younger group of reserves that includes Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese. The decision has drawn criticism from some fans, but it has not stopped the U.S. from reaching another semifinal with a 4-0 record.

Spain will enter as a significant underdog based on the countries’ history. The U.S. has won all 11 previous meetings listed by FIBA, including the 2014 World Cup championship game and the gold-medal game at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

The Americans have also won 34 consecutive World Cup games since losing to Russia in the 2006 semifinals. They are two victories away from claiming a fifth straight World Cup championship.

Spain, meanwhile, is back in the tournament after failing to qualify in 2022. The country has won three World Cup medals but has never captured gold.

Saturday’s semifinal will begin at 6 p.m. local time in Berlin. DiLeo will be trying to lead Spain to its first victory over the U.S., even if doing so requires eliminating the player she once helped bring to Iowa.

item.title: WATCH: Socialist protester blames 'provocateurs' after assaults at 'closest entry point' to Trump convention
item.description: A socialist protester blamed right-wing provocateurs after Dallas police in riot gear arrested two near the Republican National Committee convention.
item.content:encoded:
A socialist "Never Trumpers" protester blamed "conservative provocateurs" for a tense confrontation with police that resulted in multiple arrests just outside the Republican National Committee's midterm convention in Dallas.

Videos posted on social media Thursday afternoon showed what appeared to be hundreds of Never Trumpers confronting Dallas police just blocks from where the president was set to deliver his convention-closing speech. Authorities responded with a strong show of force that included officers in apparent riot gear.

The Dallas Police Department confirmed with Fox News Digital that two protesters were arrested on charges related to their actions during the protest. The department said that officers assigned to the area arrested the two protesters after it said they "assaulted a counter-protester" and "obstructed a road."

The department said the suspects’ names and specific charges will be released after they are booked into jail.

CAN THE 'BEST SHOWMAN IN POLITICS' DELIVER AGAIN? GOP BETS ON TRUMP AT HISTORIC MIDTERM CONVENTION

Fox News Digital spoke with a protester named Rick Majumdar, who was wearing a shirt with the initials for the Freedom Road Socialist Organization (FRSO), which, according to its website, is a "national organization of revolutionaries fighting for socialism in the United States."

Majumdar said that the protest was organized by the Dallas Against the Trump Agenda Coalition, which, he said, consists of 16 "faith-based organizations, pro-immigrants’ rights groups and labor organizations."

"We're here to protest the Republican agenda, the Trump agenda and all its policies that it has enacted over the last few years," he explained. "The march is an important event, we feel, against this convention that's happening for the last two days."

REPUBLICANS HEAD TO DALLAS WITH ONE MISSION: DEFY HISTORY AND WIN BIG

He said that, during the group's march, "we encountered some street closures by the police" and that officers arrested a couple of protesters who "were at the front of the group."

Pressed on why the protesters were arrested, Majumdar said, "Those people were trying to draw people away from rioting provocateurs, and I think the police heard something. And they immediately tackled two of them and arrested them, and some of them even pulled out their guns as well."

The protest came amid heightened concerns over political violence and the targeting of public figures. It also coincided with the first anniversary of the assassination of conservative activist and Turning Point USA co-founder Charlie Kirk.

CHARLIE KIRK CONTINUES TO INSPIRE REPUBLICANS AS PARTY RALLIES FOR MIDTERM BATTLE: 'HAVE COURAGE'

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Majumdar did not answer whether the protesters blocked any roads but said the confrontation occurred at the "closest entry point" to the convention.

Asked whether he had any message directly for President Donald Trump, Majumdar paused, smiled and said, "Thank you."

After publication, Freedom Road Socialist Organization shared an additional statement from Majumdar in response to Fox News Digital's question on his direct message to Trump. 

The statement said that "today the people of Dallas marched on a near empty RNC, in fact, the people made their decision to stand against the billionaires class— the same class that supports the Republican Agenda, and we are empowering people to find their home in our organization."

item.title: Franklin Graham calls on America to 'turn back' to God 25 years after 9/11: 'We still need His help today'
item.description: Franklin Graham urges America to rediscover the faith that filled churches after 9/11 as the nation marks 25 years since the terrorist attacks.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Rev. Franklin Graham is calling on Americans to remember the extraordinary turn toward faith that followed the 9/11 terrorist attacks and to "turn back" to God as the nation marks 25 years since the day that changed the world forever.

"September 11 is a day I’ll never forget," Graham, president and CEO of the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association (BGEA) and Samaritan’s Purse, told Fox News Digital.

"It’s impossible to describe the tremendous amount of pain that I witnessed at Ground Zero in the aftermath. There were so many who were in shock and grieving," he added. "It is still hard to fathom the depths of evil that caused so much destruction."

As Americans commemorate a quarter-century since the attacks, Graham said his prayer is for America to rediscover her reliance on faith he witnessed in the aftermath.

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: 9/11 IS JUST A HISTORY CHAPTER FOR A NEW GENERATION OF AMERICANS

"As we observe the 25th anniversary of this day when our world changed forever, my prayer is that America will recognize our need for God like we did after 9/11," Graham said. "Churches were full. People gathered to pray in public places."

Graham also recalled his father, the late evangelist Rev. Billy Graham, addressing the country from Washington National Cathedral during a national day of prayer and remembrance following the attacks.

"We’ve always needed God from the very beginning of this nation. But today we need Him especially," Billy Graham said at the time, according to Graham’s statement. "We’re involved in a new kind of warfare. And we need the help of the Spirit of God."

GEORGE BUSH WELCOMES TOP OFFICIALS TO HIS HOME STATE FOR 9/11 REMEMBRANCE ON 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF ATTACKS

"Just as America needed the help of God then, we still need His help today," Franklin Graham said.

Those themes are at the center of BGEA’s new 30-minute program, "A Day That Changed Our Lives Forever," hosted by Graham and featuring survivors reflecting on the attacks and the faith and hope they say emerged from the devastation.

Among them is Genelle Guzman-McMillan, the last person pulled alive from the World Trade Center rubble.

Guzman-McMillan spent 27 hours buried beneath the ruins, unable to move and unsure whether she would survive.

While trapped, she said she began thinking about her late mother and crying out to God for forgiveness and a second chance.

FOX NEWS MEDIA ANNOUNCES EXTENSIVE 9/11 ANNIVERSARY COVERAGE FROM GROUND ZERO, PENTAGON AND SHANKSVILLE

At one point, Guzman-McMillan said she could no longer endure it.

"God, are you listening to me? Please show me a sign," she recalled saying. Then something happened she still cannot explain.

"And then someone grabbed me by my hand," Guzman-McMillan says in the special. "He told me his name is Paul."

She said Paul held her hand and reassured her.

SALVATION ARMY RESPONDER OPENS UP ON 9/11 CANCER BATTLE, PHONE CALL THAT CHANGED HIS LIFE

"You’re gonna be fine. Help is on the way. I’m not gonna let you go," she recalled him saying.

As Guzman-McMillan began hearing rescuers’ radios, she said Paul encouraged her to keep calling out. Eventually, she heard a rescuer say, "I see her."

"I just knew I was going to go home," she said. "I am the last survivor, buried for 27 hours. I myself couldn’t believe that I survived it."

Guzman-McMillan said she believes the mysterious Paul was "an angel looking out for me."

"I wasn’t hallucinating, I wasn’t dreaming," she said. "I knew the conversation that I had."

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

"Something happened under that rubble," she added. "I found Jesus that day."

The special features another dramatic survival story from Sujo John, a father-to-be who worked on the 81st floor of the North Tower while his pregnant wife worked on the 71st floor of the South Tower.

After escaping, he spent hours believing his wife had died. Then his cellphone rang.

"I picked up that call thinking this is going to be the worst news of my life," he recalled.

9/11 HERO’S MEMORY PRESERVED THROUGH MASSIVE EFFORT TO ‘DO GOOD’ FOR VETS, FIRST RESPONDERS: ‘HIS LEGACY’

His wife was on the other end. She had been late for work by just minutes.

"She thought I was dead," he said. The two arranged a meeting place and ran toward each other. "We both survived."

Graham also recounted traveling to New York after the attacks and seeing people holding photographs of missing loved ones and desperately seeking information.

He began calling pastors and asking them to come help comfort and pray with grieving families.

FRANK SILLER: 'I LOVE YOU, BROTHER' — THE 9/11 LOSS THAT INSPIRED A MISSION OF SERVICE

That response ultimately led Graham to form the Billy Graham Rapid Response Team, which BGEA says has grown into an international network of thousands of crisis-trained chaplains who minister to people facing emotional and spiritual needs following tragedies and disasters.

Graham hosts "A Day That Changed Our Lives Forever," airing on Fox News Channel at 12:30 a.m. ET.

Twenty-five years later, Graham said his prayer for America remains clear.

"My prayer for our nation is that we will turn back to the God of Heaven who has brought us to this day and sustained us every step of the way."

item.title: Popular cruise line shuts down fan-favorite amenity during health scare
item.description: All public hot tubs and balcony whirlpools on Norwegian Prima remain closed as water testing continues after three Legionnaires' disease cases.
item.content:encoded:
A cruise line reportedly shut down hot tubs and heated whirlpools aboard one of its ships as a precaution after three confirmed cases of Legionnaires' disease involving former passengers.

The cases involved three travelers who sailed aboard Norwegian Prima, a 3,200-passenger vessel, in May and July 2026, the blog Cruise Fever reported.

The source of the exposure has not yet been determined.

CRUISE SHIPS WITH THE WORST CDC SANITATION SCORES REVEALED; SEE WHICH VESSELS FAILED INSPECTION

"We can confirm that three guests who sailed aboard one of our ships recently were diagnosed with Legionnaires’ disease following their travels," a spokesperson for Norwegian Cruise Line told Fox News Digital this week. 

"While it has not been confirmed if the exposure occurred on the ship or elsewhere, we are working closely with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to investigate these cases, as well as mitigate any further incidents, and have notified the appropriate guests and crew directly per the CDC’s guidance," the spokesperson added.

"We have elevated our sanitation procedures as part of our routine measures to ensure a safe environment on board and will continue to take any necessary measures to protect our guests and crew," the spokesperson continued.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Legionnaires' disease is a type of pneumonia caused by Legionella bacteria, which can spread when people inhale small water droplets containing the bacteria.

It can pose a greater risk to those over 50, current or former smokers and people with chronic lung disease or weakened immune systems.

The cruise line said the ship's hot tubs and heated whirlpools would remain closed as a precaution while testing continues, according to the Cruise Fever report. 

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"As a precaution, all public hot tubs and private balcony heated whirlpools will remain closed and will reopen only after sampling has been completed and any necessary remediation measures have been carried out in accordance with CDC guidelines," the blog noted.

Online, people shared mixed reactions. 

"Stay out of the hot tub, the bacteria thrives in hot tubs! It's not transferable from person to person," one person wrote.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I have never, nor will I ever, get in a public hot tub," said another Reddit user. "I’ve been on over 20 cruises and have never gotten in a single pool or hot tub on one. No, thank you!" 

"I booked this cruise over a year ago. So I'm pretty much going no matter what," the original poster wrote. "Can't say I feel great about it, though."

"The health and safety of our guests and crew is our top priority. As such, we operate at the very highest public health and sanitation standards," the Norwegian Cruise Line spokesperson added.
